questions.q: Which resume bullet best follows the action verb + what you built + quantified outcome formula?
options: Learned about CI/CD pipelines and Kubernetes
Familiar with Terraform and Azure
Configured Kubernetes HPAs for two services, scaling checkout from 3 to 15 pods at 70% CPU
Worked on a DevOps project with a team
questions.explain: This bullet names the action (configured), the real mechanism (HPAs for two services), and a quantified outcome (3 to 15 pods, 70% CPU) instead of vague exposure language.

questions.q: What makes 'Worked on CI/CD' a weak resume bullet?
options: It is too long
It names a topic instead of a real mechanism or outcome
It uses too many numbers
It is grammatically incorrect
questions.explain: Strong bullets name the specific thing you built and a quantified result; naming only the topic reads like a tutorial, not real experience.

questions.q: What is the recommended pattern for a DevOps-focused LinkedIn headline?
options: Current job title only
A list of every technology ever touched
Role plus 3-4 core tools plus one differentiator
A motivational quote
questions.explain: A headline that names the target role, a handful of real tools, and a differentiator (like the capstone) is far more scannable than a generic title or an exhaustive tool list.

questions.q: Where should a candidate place their portfolio repository on LinkedIn for maximum visibility?
options: Nowhere — repos don't belong on LinkedIn
Only in the Education section
In the Featured section, pinned under the headline
In a private message to recruiters only
questions.explain: The Featured section sits near the top of a profile and is one of the first things a recruiter or hiring manager clicks, making it the best place for a pinned portfolio repo.

questions.q: Which capstone detail gives a candidate a real, quantified resume bullet rather than a vague claim?
options: "Used monitoring tools"
"Traced checkout p99 latency rising from ~400ms to 6.2s to a saturated DB connection pool using Prometheus and the USE method"
"Interested in observability"
"Has seen a Grafana dashboard before"
questions.explain: This bullet names the specific numbers (400ms to 6.2s), the real tools (Prometheus), and the real method (USE) from the capstone's incident drill.
